revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Biology
revealWordProblem.text: James is studying the growth rate of a specific type of bacteria. He places three cells in a Petri dish and records the number of bacteria every five hours. His results are: 0 hours → 3 bacteria, 5 hours → 9 bacteria, 10 hours → 27 bacteria, 15 hours → 81 bacteria. Choose a question to answer. Question 1: The counts 3, 9, 27, 81 are powers of which base, and what power represents each new 5-hour reading? Question 2: What power would represent the number of bacteria after 25 hours, and what is its value?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The counts are powers of 3: 3 = 3¹, 9 = 3², 27 = 3³, 81 = 3⁴, so each 5-hour reading raises the exponent by 1. After 25 hours that is the 6th reading, so it is 3⁶ = 729 bacteria.

turnAndTalk.question: In the sound studio, the volume doubles each time you flip the switch. Why is the volume after 3 flips 2³ = 8 and not 2 × 3 = 6?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The exponent counts how many times we multiply, not what we add.

stems.en: After 3 flips the volume is ___ because we multiply 2 three times.
stems.es: Después de 3 cambios el volumen es ___ porque multiplicamos 2 tres veces.

stems.en: It is not 6 because doubling means we ___, not add.
stems.es: No es 6 porque duplicar significa que ___, no sumar.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students connect each switch flip to one more factor of 2 and explain that 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, distinguishing repeated multiplication from repeated addition (which would give 6).
turnAndTalk.extend: If the volume tripled instead of doubled each flip, how would you write the volume after 3 flips, and how many times louder would that be than the doubling case?
extendStems: Tripling gives ___ = ___, which is ___ times the doubling result because ___.
Changing the base from 2 to 3 matters more than changing the exponent because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Look at the table: when the exponent goes up by 1 (like from 2³ to 2⁴), what happens to the value, and why?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Each time the exponent grows by 1, the value is multiplied by the base one more time.

stems.en: When the exponent increases by 1, the value is multiplied by ___.
stems.es: Cuando el exponente aumenta en 1, el valor se multiplica por ___.

stems.en: This happens because the base is used as a factor ___ more time.
stems.es: Esto pasa porque la base se usa como factor ___ vez más.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer states that the value gets multiplied by the base (e.g., 2³ = 8 becomes 2⁴ = 16, times 2) and ties it to adding one more factor, using the words base and exponent.
turnAndTalk.extend: Compare 2⁵ and 5². Both use the digits 2 and 5, so why are they not equal? Generalize: does the bigger exponent or the bigger base have more effect on the value?
extendStems: 2⁵ = ___ but 5² = ___, so they are not equal because ___.
In general, a larger ___ has more effect because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Each recording layer doubles the file size, modeled by 4 × 2ⁿ. Why does the file size grow so fast as you add layers?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Doubling repeatedly is exponential growth, so the size explodes after only a few layers.

stems.en: After 5 layers the file is ___ MB because 4 × 2⁵ = ___.
stems.es: Después de 5 capas el archivo es ___ MB porque 4 × 2⁵ = ___.

stems.en: It grows quickly because each layer ___ the size.
stems.es: Crece rápido porque cada capa ___ el tamaño.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students evaluate 4 × 2⁵ = 4 × 32 = 128 MB and explain that exponential (doubling) growth multiplies the size each step, unlike adding a fixed amount.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique this claim: 'After 10 layers the file is just twice as big as after 5 layers.' Is that true? Justify with the powers involved.
extendStems: The claim is ___ because 2¹⁰ compared to 2⁵ is ___, not just doubled.
Exponential growth means going from 5 to 10 layers multiplies the size by ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Powers and Exponents, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A power like 2³ is a short way to write repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2.

stems.en: When a problem felt tricky, I ___ to figure it out.
stems.es: Cuando un problema fue difícil, yo ___ para resolverlo.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.5 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

conceptIntro.heading: What does an exponent mean?
conceptIntro.intro: An exponent is a small raised number that tells you how many times to multiply a number by itself. We say 2³ as "two to the third power."
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A power like 2³ is a short way to write repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want to find the value of 2³.
The small 3 tells me to multiply 2 by itself 3 times.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's find 5². How many times do we multiply 5 by itself?
The exponent is 2, so we write 5 × 5.

optionalActivity.name: Exponent Beat Builder
optionalActivity.intro: Lay down beat tracks in the studio: each stage layers in powers, repeated multiplication, and values to build the loop.

optional.stem: The drum loop plays 3⁴ beats. What is the value of 3⁴?
optional.explanation: 3⁴ means use 3 as a factor 4 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. It is NOT 3 × 4 = 12.
choiceFeedback: Did you multiply the base by the exponent instead? Try: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3.
Check the value. Is 7 anywhere in this power?
That's 3³. Count how many 3's to multiply in 3⁴.
optional.stemEs: El bucle de batería toca 3⁴ tiempos. ¿Cuál es el valor de 3⁴?
optional.explanationEs: 3⁴ significa usar 3 como factor 4 veces: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. NO es 3 × 4 = 12.
hints: In a power, the small raised number counts how many times the base is used as a factor — it is not something you multiply by.
Write the power out as repeated multiplication before you compute anything.
3⁴ means 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiply the first two to get 9, then keep multiplying by 3 for each factor that is left.
hintsEs: En una potencia, el número pequeño de arriba cuenta cuántas veces se usa la base como factor; no es algo por lo que se multiplica.
Escribe la potencia como multiplicación repetida antes de calcular nada.
3⁴ significa 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiplica los dos primeros para obtener 9 y sigue multiplicando por 3 con cada factor que queda.

optional.stem: A synth pattern repeats 7 × 7 × 7. How do you write that as a power?
optional.explanation: The base 7 is used as a factor 3 times, so the power is 7³. 7³ = 7 × 7 × 7 = 343.
choiceFeedback: You switched base and exponent. The base repeats; the exponent counts times.
You wrote 7 times 3, but the exponent tells you how many 7's to multiply.
That mixes the base with the exponent. What's the base, and how many times does it repeat?
optional.stemEs: Un patrón de sintetizador repite 7 × 7 × 7. ¿Cómo se escribe eso como una potencia?
optional.explanationEs: La base 7 se usa como factor 3 veces, así que la potencia es 7³. 7³ = 7 × 7 × 7 = 343.
hints: A power has two parts: the base is the number being repeated, and the exponent tells how many times it appears.
Find the repeated number first, then count how many times it shows up in the multiplication.
The number 7 is the one being repeated, so 7 is the base. Now count the 7s in 7 × 7 × 7 and put that count in the exponent position.
hintsEs: Una potencia tiene dos partes: la base es el número que se repite y el exponente indica cuántas veces aparece.
Primero identifica el número que se repite y luego cuenta cuántas veces aparece en la multiplicación.
El número 7 es el que se repite, así que 7 es la base. Ahora cuenta los 7 en 7 × 7 × 7 y coloca ese conteo en la posición del exponente.

optional.stem: The bass line doubles for 2⁶ counts. What is the value of 2⁶?
optional.explanation: 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64. The exponent 6 counts how many times 2 is a factor.
choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent? Try writing 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2.
That's 2⁵. Count the factors: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2.
Check your addition. Is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 36?
optional.stemEs: La línea de bajo se duplica durante 2⁶ tiempos. ¿Cuál es el valor de 2⁶?
optional.explanationEs: 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64. El exponente 6 cuenta cuántas veces el 2 es un factor.
hints: The exponent 6 tells you how many 2s get multiplied together — it does not mean 2 × 6.
Write out six 2s multiplied in a row, then work from left to right.
Start doubling: 2 × 2 = 4, then 4 × 2 = 8. Keep doubling until all six factors have been used.
hintsEs: El exponente 6 te dice cuántos 2 se multiplican entre sí; no significa 2 × 6.
Escribe seis 2 multiplicados en fila y luego trabaja de izquierda a derecha.
Empieza a duplicar: 2 × 2 = 4, luego 4 × 2 = 8. Sigue duplicando hasta usar los seis factores.

optional.instructions: Drag each repeated-multiplication beat next to its matching exponential form.
optional.explanation: Match by counting factors, not by size. 7 × 7 × 7 has three 7's, so it is 7³; 6 × 6 has two 6's, so it is 6²; 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 has four 4's, so it is 4⁴; and 9 × 9 has two 9's, so it is 9². The repeated number becomes the base and how many times it appears becomes the exponent.
optional.explanationEs: Empareja contando factores, no por tamaño. 7 × 7 × 7 tiene tres 7, así que es 7³; 6 × 6 tiene dos 6, así que es 6²; 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 tiene cuatro 4, así que es 4⁴; y 9 × 9 tiene dos 9, así que es 9². El número que se repite es la base y la cantidad de veces que aparece es el exponente.
hints: You are not evaluating anything here — each card just needs the exponential form that says the same thing.
In each card, the number being repeated becomes the base, and how many times it appears becomes the exponent.
Take 4 × 4 × 4 × 4: the repeated number is 4, so count how many 4's you see and look for the label with that exponent.
hintsEs: Aquí no estás calculando nada: cada tarjeta solo necesita la forma exponencial que dice lo mismo.
En cada tarjeta, el número que se repite es la base y la cantidad de veces que aparece es el exponente.
Toma 4 × 4 × 4 × 4: el número que se repite es 4, así que cuenta cuántos 4 ves y busca la etiqueta con ese exponente.
optional.instructionsEs: Arrastra cada ritmo de multiplicación repetida junto a su forma exponencial correspondiente.

optional.label: Match each power to the number of beats it plays (its value).
optional.explanation: Expanding each power gives its beat count: 7³ = 343, 6² = 36, 4⁴ = 256, 9² = 81, 6³ = 216, and 7² = 49. The pairs that share a base are the ones to check closely — 7² = 49 while 7³ = 343, and 6² = 36 while 6³ = 216 — because one extra factor multiplies the value by the base again.
optional.explanationEs: Al desarrollar cada potencia se obtiene su cantidad de tiempos: 7³ = 343, 6² = 36, 4⁴ = 256, 9² = 81, 6³ = 216 y 7² = 49. Las parejas que comparten la base son las que hay que revisar con cuidado —7² = 49 mientras que 7³ = 343, y 6² = 36 mientras que 6³ = 216— porque un factor adicional vuelve a multiplicar el valor por la base.
hints: The exponent counts how many times the base is used as a factor, so a power with a small base can still produce a big number of beats.
Evaluate the squares first — 6², 9², 7² — to clear away the smaller values, then work out the powers with exponent 3 or 4.
Start with 7³: multiply 7 × 7 = 49, then multiply that result by 7 one more time and look for the card that matches.
hintsEs: El exponente cuenta cuántas veces se usa la base como factor, así que una potencia con base pequeña todavía puede dar muchos tiempos.
Calcula primero los cuadrados —6², 9², 7²— para descartar los valores pequeños y luego resuelve las potencias con exponente 3 o 4.
Empieza con 7³: multiplica 7 × 7 = 49, luego multiplica ese resultado por 7 una vez más y busca la tarjeta que coincida.
optional.labelEs: Une cada potencia con la cantidad de tiempos que toca (su valor).

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Spot the Beat-Builder Bug
optional.correctWork: 3⁴ does NOT mean 3 × 4. The exponent 4 tells you to use the base 3 as a factor 4 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. So the track plays 81 beats, not 12.
hints: Does the exponent tell you to multiply the base BY the exponent, or to use the base as a factor that many times?
Write 3⁴ as repeated multiplication first: 3 × 3 × ___ × ___, then multiply step by step.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Encuentra la falla del constructor de ritmos
optional.explanation: The "Producer's thinking" step reads 3⁴ as 3 × 4, which multiplies by the exponent instead of counting factors. The 4 means the base 3 is used four times: 3 × 3 = 9, 9 × 3 = 27, 27 × 3 = 81. The track plays 81 beats, not 12.
optional.explanationEs: El paso "Producer's thinking" lee 3⁴ como 3 × 4, lo que multiplica por el exponente en vez de contar factores. El 4 significa que la base 3 se usa cuatro veces: 3 × 3 = 9, 9 × 3 = 27, 27 × 3 = 81. La pista toca 81 tiempos, no 12.
optional.correctWorkEs: 3⁴ NO significa 3 × 4. El exponente 4 te dice que uses la base 3 como factor 4 veces: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Así que la pista toca 81 tiempos, no 12.

choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent (4 × 3)? The exponent counts how many 4's.
Look at the power: 4³ has a 4 and a 3, but not 43.
That's not matching the repeated multiplication 4 × 4 × 4.
hints: Look at the small raised 3. That exponent counts how many 4's get multiplied — it is not a number to multiply 4 by.
Rewrite the power as repeated multiplication first, then multiply one step at a time.
Write 4³ as 4 × 4 × 4. Multiply the first pair (4 × 4 = 16), then multiply that result by the last 4.
hintsEs: Mira el pequeño 3 elevado. Ese exponente cuenta cuántos 4 se multiplican; no es un número por el que se multiplica el 4.
Reescribe primero la potencia como multiplicación repetida y luego multiplica paso a paso.
Escribe 4³ como 4 × 4 × 4. Multiplica el primer par (4 × 4 = 16) y luego multiplica ese resultado por el último 4.

choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent? Write 6 × 6 instead.
That mixes the digits. Is the power 62 or 6²?
hints: The little 2 is the exponent. It counts how many 6's you multiply — it's not a number to add or multiply by.
Turn the power into repeated multiplication before you calculate anything.
Rewrite 6² as 6 × 6, then multiply those two factors.
hintsEs: El pequeño 2 es el exponente. Cuenta cuántos 6 multiplicas; no es un número para sumar ni para multiplicar.
Convierte la potencia en multiplicación repetida antes de calcular nada.
Reescribe 6² como 6 × 6 y luego multiplica esos dos factores.

approaching.stem: Which expression shows 5³ as repeated multiplication?
approaching.explanation: 5³ means use 5 as a factor 3 times: 5 × 5 × 5. The exponent tells how many times to multiply, not what to multiply by.
choiceFeedback: The exponent tells you to multiply 5, not multiply it by 3.
Adding is different from multiplying. Exponents mean repeated multiplication.
The exponent 3 means three factors of 5, not three copies written as 3×3×3×3×3.
hints: In 5³ the base is 5 and the exponent is 3. Ask: which number repeats, and how many times?
The exponent counts the factors. Look for the base written as a factor that many times.
Say it out loud: 'use 5 as a factor 3 times.' Count the 5's in each choice — you need exactly three of them.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión muestra 5³ como una multiplicación repetida?
approaching.explanationEs: 5³ significa usar 5 como factor 3 veces: 5 × 5 × 5. El exponente indica cuántas veces se multiplica, no por cuánto se multiplica.
hintsEs: En 5³ la base es 5 y el exponente es 3. Pregunta: ¿qué número se repite y cuántas veces?
El exponente cuenta los factores. Busca la base escrita como factor esa cantidad de veces.
Dilo en voz alta: 'usa 5 como factor 3 veces'. Cuenta los 5 en cada opción: necesitas exactamente tres.

choiceFeedback: Order of operations: do the parentheses and exponent first, then multiply.
You stopped after the exponent. 6² = 36 is only the middle step — the 3 in front still has to be multiplied in.
Did you just compute 3 × 6 × 2 instead of respecting the exponent?
hints: There are three jobs here: parentheses, an exponent, and multiplication. Order of operations decides which comes first.
Do the parentheses first, then square that result, then multiply by 3 last.
Start inside: 4 + 2 = 6. Now the problem becomes 3 × 6². Handle the exponent next.
hintsEs: Aquí hay tres tareas: paréntesis, un exponente y una multiplicación. El orden de las operaciones decide qué va primero.
Haz primero el paréntesis, luego eleva ese resultado al cuadrado y al final multiplica por 3.
Empieza por dentro: 4 + 2 = 6. Ahora el problema es 3 × 6². Sigue con el exponente.

approaching.instructions: Write each power as repeated multiplication, then find the value.
hints: The middle column already shows each power as repeated multiplication — use it!
Multiply the factors left to right, two at a time, and write the final product in the Value column.
For 3², multiply 3 × 3. For 2⁴, chain it: 2 × 2 = 4, then × 2, then × 2 again.
approaching.explanation: The middle column already unpacks each power, so all that is left is to multiply. 3² means two factors of 3, and 3 × 3 = 9. 2⁴ means four factors of 2, and multiplying step by step gives 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. The exponent counts the factors; it is never one of the factors.
approaching.explanationEs: La columna del medio ya desarma cada potencia, así que solo falta multiplicar. 3² significa dos factores de 3, y 3 × 3 = 9. 2⁴ significa cuatro factores de 2, y multiplicando paso a paso da 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. El exponente cuenta los factores; nunca es uno de los factores.
approaching.instructionsEs: Escribe cada potencia como una multiplicación repetida y después encuentra su valor.
hintsEs: La columna del medio ya muestra cada potencia como multiplicación repetida: ¡úsala!
Multiplica los factores de izquierda a derecha, de dos en dos, y escribe el producto final en la columna Valor.
Para 3², multiplica 3 × 3. Para 2⁴, encadénalo: 2 × 2 = 4, luego × 2 y luego × 2 otra vez.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: 5³ does NOT mean 5 × 3. The exponent 3 tells you to use the base 5 as a factor 3 times: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. So 5³ = 125, not 15.
hints: Does the exponent tell you to multiply the base BY the exponent, or to use the base as a factor that many times?
Write 5³ as repeated multiplication first: 5 × 5 × 5, then multiply step by step.
approaching.explanation: The "Student's thinking" step rewrites 5³ as 5 × 3, treating the exponent as a factor. The exponent 3 instead tells you how many times to use the base 5 as a factor: 5 × 5 × 5. Multiplying gives 5 × 5 = 25 and 25 × 5 = 125, so 5³ = 125, not 15.
approaching.explanationEs: El paso "Student's thinking" reescribe 5³ como 5 × 3, tratando el exponente como un factor. En cambio, el exponente 3 te dice cuántas veces usar la base 5 como factor: 5 × 5 × 5. Al multiplicar da 5 × 5 = 25 y 25 × 5 = 125, así que 5³ = 125, no 15.
approaching.correctWorkEs: 5³ NO significa 5 × 3. El exponente 3 te dice que uses la base 5 como factor 3 veces: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Así que 5³ = 125, no 15.

onLevel.instructions: Evaluate each exponential expression. Show the repeated multiplication and the final value.
hints: Each row shows the repeated multiplication for you. Your job is to multiply the factors carefully.
Multiply left to right, keeping a running total. For 10⁴, watch the zeros pile up.
Row 1: 4 × 4 = 16, then 16 × 4 gives the value. Use the same running-total idea for the other rows.
onLevel.explanation: Multiply the listed factors with a running total: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, 2⁶ = 64 as well after six doublings, 5³ = 125, and 10⁴ = 10,000. Notice that 4³ and 2⁶ have the same value even though the bases and exponents differ, and that 10⁴ gains one zero for each factor of 10.
onLevel.explanationEs: Multiplica los factores que aparecen llevando un total acumulado: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, 2⁶ también da 64 después de seis duplicaciones, 5³ = 125 y 10⁴ = 10,000. Fíjate en que 4³ y 2⁶ tienen el mismo valor aunque las bases y los exponentes sean distintos, y en que 10⁴ gana un cero por cada factor de 10.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Evalúa cada expresión exponencial. Muestra la multiplicación repetida y el valor final.
hintsEs: Cada fila te muestra la multiplicación repetida. Tu trabajo es multiplicar los factores con cuidado.
Multiplica de izquierda a derecha llevando un total parcial. En 10⁴, observa cómo se acumulan los ceros.
Fila 1: 4 × 4 = 16 y luego 16 × 4 da el valor. Usa la misma idea del total parcial en las demás filas.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each power by whether its value is greater than 50 or not.
hints: Each card already shows the power's value after the equals sign — that value is what you compare to 50.
Ignore the exponent form; ask 'is this value more than 50?' Remember exactly 50 would count as ≤ 50.
Try the first card: 2⁵ = 32. Is 32 greater than 50? Place it, then test each card the same way.
onLevel.explanation: Each card already shows its value, so the sorting is a comparison with 50. Above 50 are 3⁴ = 81, 10² = 100, and 5³ = 125. At or below 50 are 2⁵ = 32, 7² = 49, and 4² = 16. Watch 7² = 49: it looks close, but 49 is less than 50, so it belongs with the smaller group.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su valor, así que clasificar es comparar con 50. Por encima de 50 están 3⁴ = 81, 10² = 100 y 5³ = 125. En 50 o por debajo están 2⁵ = 32, 7² = 49 y 4² = 16. Cuidado con 7² = 49: parece cercano, pero 49 es menor que 50, así que va en el grupo de los pequeños.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada potencia según si su valor es mayor que 50 o no.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra el valor de la potencia después del signo igual: ese valor es el que comparas con 50.
Ignora la forma con exponente; pregunta '¿es este valor más que 50?'. Recuerda que exactamente 50 cuenta como ≤ 50.
Prueba la primera tarjeta: 2⁵ = 32. ¿Es 32 mayor que 50? Colócala y prueba cada tarjeta igual.

onLevel.label: Match each power to its value.
hints: Each power hides a value. The base is the number you repeat; the exponent counts the repeats.
Evaluate each power on scrap paper first, then find its match. Do quick ones like 5² first to shrink the list.
Start with 3³: multiply 3 × 3 = 9, then 9 × 3. Match that result, then move to the next power.
onLevel.explanation: Expand each power and multiply: 2⁵ = 32, 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, 10³ = 1,000, 5² = 25, and 2⁷ = 128. The two powers of 2 are the ones most likely to be mixed up, so count factors carefully — five 2's give 32, while seven 2's give 128.
onLevel.explanationEs: Desarrolla cada potencia y multiplica: 2⁵ = 32, 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, 10³ = 1,000, 5² = 25 y 2⁷ = 128. Las dos potencias de 2 son las que más se confunden, así que cuenta bien los factores: cinco 2 dan 32, mientras que siete 2 dan 128.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada potencia con su valor.
hintsEs: Cada potencia esconde un valor. La base es el número que se repite; el exponente cuenta las repeticiones.
Evalúa cada potencia en papel primero y luego busca su pareja. Haz las fáciles como 5² primero para acortar la lista.
Empieza con 3³: multiplica 3 × 3 = 9 y luego 9 × 3. Une ese resultado y pasa a la siguiente potencia.

onLevel.instructions: Which side is greater? Evaluate each expression. Left: 3⁴. Right: 4³.
onLevel.label: Compare: 3⁴ vs. 4³
onLevel.hint: Evaluate 3⁴ and 4³ separately by writing repeated multiplication, then compare values.
hints: Don't guess — a bigger base doesn't always win. Compare the actual values of 3⁴ and 4³.
Write each side as repeated multiplication: four 3's for 3⁴, three 4's for 4³. Then multiply each out.
Left side first: 3 × 3 = 9, then 9 × 3 = 27, then × 3 once more. Next do 4 × 4 × 4 and compare.
onLevel.explanation: 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81 and 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so the left side is greater and the scale tips toward 3⁴. The bigger base does not automatically win — here the extra factor on the left outweighs the larger base on the right.
onLevel.explanationEs: 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81 y 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, así que el lado izquierdo es mayor y la balanza se inclina hacia 3⁴. La base más grande no gana automáticamente: aquí el factor adicional de la izquierda pesa más que la base mayor de la derecha.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 2⁴ does NOT mean 2 × 4. The exponent 4 tells you to use the base 2 as a factor 4 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16. So 2⁴ = 16, not 8.
hints: Count how many 2's you should multiply: the exponent 4 means four factors of 2.
Write 2⁴ as repeated multiplication first: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2, then multiply step by step.
onLevel.explanation: The "Student's thinking" step turns 2⁴ into 2 × 4. The exponent 4 is a count, not a factor: it says to use the base 2 four times, giving 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Doubling step by step gives 2, 4, 8, 16, so 2⁴ = 16, not 8.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Student's thinking" convierte 2⁴ en 2 × 4. El exponente 4 es una cuenta, no un factor: indica usar la base 2 cuatro veces, o sea 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Duplicando paso a paso da 2, 4, 8, 16, así que 2⁴ = 16, no 8.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 2⁴ NO significa 2 × 4. El exponente 4 te dice que uses la base 2 como factor 4 veces: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16. Así que 2⁴ = 16, no 8.

extending.title: Find the Exponent Error
extending.correctWork: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2, NOT 2 × 3. The exponent tells us to multiply the base by itself 3 times: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
hints: Does the exponent mean to multiply the base BY the exponent, or to multiply the base BY ITSELF that many times?
Write out what 2³ means as repeated multiplication: 2 × ___ × ___.
extending.explanation: The "Student's thinking" step reads 2³ as 2 × 3, which is multiplication by the exponent rather than repeated multiplication of the base. Written correctly, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2, so 2 × 2 = 4 and 4 × 2 = 8. The value is 8, not 6.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Student's thinking" lee 2³ como 2 × 3, lo que es multiplicar por el exponente en lugar de multiplicar la base repetidamente. Escrito correctamente, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2, así que 2 × 2 = 4 y 4 × 2 = 8. El valor es 8, no 6.
extending.correctWorkEs: 2³ significa 2 × 2 × 2, NO 2 × 3. El exponente nos dice que multipliquemos la base por sí misma 3 veces: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

extending.prompt: A bacteria colony doubles every hour. Starting with 1 bacterium, write a power expression for the number after 6 hours. Explain why exponential growth is so much faster than adding the same number each hour.
extending.sentenceFrame: After 6 hours there are ___ bacteria because 2⁶ = ___. If it grew by adding 2 each hour instead, there would only be ___ bacteria. Exponential growth is faster because ___.
extending.hint: Start by writing 2⁶ as repeated multiplication and computing its value.
hints: Doubling every hour means multiplying by 2 again and again — that's exactly what an exponent shows.
Write a power with base 2 whose exponent matches the 6 hours. Also find the adding-2-each-hour total to compare.
Expand: 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Double step by step — 2, 4, 8, … — until you've used all six factors.
extending.explanation: Doubling every hour means multiplying by 2 once per hour, so after 6 hours the count is 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64 bacteria. Adding 2 each hour instead would give only 1 + 12 = 13. Repeated multiplication compounds — each hour multiplies everything already there — while repeated addition only ever adds the same fixed amount.
extending.explanationEs: Duplicarse cada hora significa multiplicar por 2 una vez por hora, así que después de 6 horas la cantidad es 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64 bacterias. Sumar 2 cada hora daría apenas 1 + 12 = 13. La multiplicación repetida se acumula —cada hora multiplica todo lo que ya existe—, mientras que la suma repetida siempre agrega la misma cantidad fija.
extending.promptEs: Una colonia de bacterias se duplica cada hora. Empezando con 1 bacteria, escribe una expresión con potencias para la cantidad después de 6 horas. Explica por qué el crecimiento exponencial es mucho más rápido que sumar la misma cantidad cada hora.
hintsEs: Duplicarse cada hora significa multiplicar por 2 una y otra vez: eso es exactamente lo que muestra un exponente.
Escribe una potencia de base 2 cuyo exponente coincida con las 6 horas. Halla también el total de sumar 2 cada hora para comparar.
Desarrolla: 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Duplica paso a paso —2, 4, 8, …— hasta usar los seis factores.

extending.instructions: Compare the values when the base and exponent are swapped. What do you notice?
hints: Swapping base and exponent changes the meaning: 2⁵ is five 2's multiplied, but 5² is only two 5's.
Evaluate each expression separately as repeated multiplication, then compare the two values in each row.
Row 1: 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 — multiply step by step. Then do 5 × 5 and compare which is greater.
extending.explanation: Swapping the base and exponent usually changes the value: 2⁵ = 32 beats 5² = 25, and 3⁴ = 81 beats 4³ = 64. The middle row is the exception — 2⁴ = 16 and 4² = 16 are equal — which shows that a swap only happens to match in special cases, not as a rule.
extending.explanationEs: Intercambiar la base y el exponente casi siempre cambia el valor: 2⁵ = 32 supera a 5² = 25, y 3⁴ = 81 supera a 4³ = 64. La fila del medio es la excepción —2⁴ = 16 y 4² = 16 son iguales—, lo que muestra que un intercambio solo coincide en casos especiales, no como regla.
extending.instructionsEs: Compara los valores cuando se intercambian la base y el exponente. ¿Qué observas?
hintsEs: Intercambiar base y exponente cambia el significado: 2⁵ son cinco 2 multiplicados, pero 5² son solo dos 5.
Evalúa cada expresión por separado como multiplicación repetida y luego compara los dos valores de cada fila.
Fila 1: 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 — multiplica paso a paso. Luego haz 5 × 5 y compara cuál es mayor.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Powers and Exponents is multiplying the base by the exponent instead of using the base as a repeated factor — for example, thinking 2³ = 2 × 3 = 6 instead of 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. Before you submit, rewrite the power as repeated multiplication first, then multiply step by step.

diagram.title: File Size Doubles Each Layer
diagram.caption: Each bar is 4 × 2ⁿ MB; every layer doubles the height, so the file races to 128 MB after 5 layers.

connect.scenario: A music studio is recording tracks. Each track layer doubles the file size. A single track is 4 MB. The file size after n layers is given by 4 × 2ⁿ.
connect.promptQuestion: How large is the file after 5 layers? Why does the file size grow so quickly?
connect.prompt: After 5 layers the file is ___ MB because 4 × 2⁵ = 4 × ___ = ___. The file grows quickly because each layer ___ the size.

check.stem: How big is the file after 5 layers?
Why does the file grow so quickly?
choices: Because each layer doubles the size instead of adding a fixed amount
Because the studio records faster each time
check.explanation: Repeated doubling is exponential growth: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Each step multiplies rather than adds, so the jumps get bigger and bigger.

connect.modelAnswer: 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32, so 4 × 2⁵ = 4 × 32 = 128 MB after 5 layers. The size grows so fast because every layer doubles it — that is exponential growth, not repeated addition.

exitTicket.explanation: 3⁴ means use 3 as a factor 4 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Choosing 12 means you multiplied the base by the exponent (3 × 4) instead of repeating the base as a factor. Choosing 34 means you just wrote the base and exponent digits side by side instead of evaluating. Choosing 64 mixes up this base and exponent with 4³ (4 × 4 × 4 = 64).
choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent (3 × 4)? The exponent counts factors.
The power is 3⁴, not 34. Write 3 × 3 × 3 × 3.
That's 4³ = 64, not 3⁴.
hints: The base is 3 and the exponent is 4. The exponent counts how many 3's to multiply — it's not 3 × 4.
Rewrite the power as repeated multiplication before picking a choice.
Write 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiply: 3 × 3 = 9, then keep multiplying by 3 two more times.

mission.title: The Doubling Mixboard
mission.story: You are the lead sound engineer at Amplitude Studios. Every time you flip a switch on the new mixboard, the volume doubles — that is the power of exponents. The headline act goes on in one hour, and you must master powers before the speakers can be safely dialed in.
mission.objective: Evaluate powers as repeated multiplication so you can predict the volume at every switch flip.

scenes.name: Sound Check
scenes.text: Flip the switch and watch the volume double from 1 unit to 2³ = 8 units.

scenes.name: Console Terms
scenes.text: Learn the studio's vocabulary: base, exponent, power, evaluate.

scenes.name: Gain Stage
scenes.text: Evaluate each power as repeated multiplication to set the right gain.

scenes.name: Mixing Session
scenes.text: Work the power problems. The console adapts the difficulty to keep you in the pocket.

scenes.name: Track Bounce
scenes.text: Use powers to predict how file size grows as you double the track layers.

scenes.name: Final Mix
scenes.text: Lock the master fader and show the studio you command exponents.

finale.title: Master Mix Locked!
finale.text: The volume hit the perfect level and the show was a sellout. Amplitude Studios just made you head engineer — because you can evaluate any power in your sleep.
